summary: Umatilla NF, Asotin County, WA; 20-foot L-4 tower built 1932 that has long since departed; footing and tent-site rock outline noted in 2016 photos; drive-up.

facts.design: 20-foot round native timber tower with L-4 observation cabin (1932)
facts.status_note: The tower has long since departed. The Willhite page says visitors can see the footing and the outhouse, and it notes that a rock outline around the tent was still there in 2016.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS register and FireLookout.com give 5,840 ft (1,780 m); the Willhite page header gives 5,900 feet. The story uses 5,840 ft (1,780 m), which matches the brief.

A 1965 newspaper item quoted on the Weebly page describes a road for construction of the Saddle Butte Lookout, while the other sources date the tower to 1932 and say it has departed. The item does not say whether a new tower was built, so the story keeps 1932 and reports the item as it stands. The road length also differs: 1.6 miles in the 1965 item and 1.7 miles on the Willhite page.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: lat 46.06915 matches firetower.org (N 46.069150); the FireLookout.org county list gives 46.06909, a small difference that is not in the facts. Height 6.1 m matches the 20-foot pole. Access was 'unknown' in the brief; filled from the Willhite drive-up description. The 1965 road item is the open question: it may mean a second lookout was planned or built, and no source confirms it. The Weebly page also shows a bare 'Removed' label beside a National Geodetic Survey block with no date; it was not used. One WebSearch used.
